structural_decomposition_at_k8.claim_boundary: Oracle uses publisher answer after generation and is NOT deployable. The 52/500 oracle-selector gap is only a bound, not a realized gain. 215/500 had no correct sampled candidate and require candidate-generation/reasoning changes, not just choosing a different sampled answer.

decision.preferred_cost_sensitive_exploratory_bas: K4 on fixed Qwen3.5-9B, same SQLite-result plurality
decision.accuracy_oriented_exploratory_baseline: K8 for no-cost-constraint maximum observed DEV accuracy only
decision.reason: K4 captures 22/30 of the observed K8 net gain over K1; K8 adds eight net correct for +7.71 measured original Qwen CPU-hours with task-level CI including zero and two-sided exact McNemar p>0.05.
decision.next_research_question: Can a preregistered, gold-blind selector recover part of the 52/500 oracle selection gap without increasing original Qwen calls or tuning on DEV500?
decision.validation_gate: Freeze selector features and thresholds on disjoint TRAIN source; reserve independent final evaluation. A source-local DEV500 comparison is diagnostic, not out-of-source proof.

limitations: Original Qwen generations were physically produced once, 32 immutable cache shards. Cumulative wall-summed CPU generation hours include first-call warmup overhead and are NOT financial cost estimates.
Original results use a special uniformly 8-second-bounded SQLite set-result comparison, not the old unbounded BIRD official evaluator.
All 11 physical DEV databases have appeared in previous project evaluations, so this is not database-disjoint generalization.
500 DEV examples are not 500 independent source databases; cluster bootstrap only has 11 DB units.
One publisher/reference query hit the bounded time limit, but every model candidate for that question was nonexecuting; it is certified wrong without inferring a gold result.
K4 vs K8 source-data selection is exploratory and may reflect tuning on DEV; do not directly promote to final test or claim a broader semantic breakthrough.
